My employer's group cover is sufficient, so I don't need a personal health insurance policy.

chain.why: This shows that the coverage you have is tied to your employer's group policy and is not automatically yours.
It indicates that even when you try to transfer the cover to your own name, the insurer may apply underwriting and could deny you.
If you cannot migrate the group cover, any new personal policy you buy will start its waiting periods from zero.
The waiting period for a declared pre‑existing condition can be as long as three years, leaving you uncovered for that time.

conclusion: Because employer cover ends with the job and a new personal policy may impose up to three‑year waiting periods, relying only on the group policy leaves you exposed to gaps in coverage.
